    if abs(ex) < 0.7 and abs(ey) < 0.7 and abs(dz) < 1.0: break
    step("right", max(-20, min(20, ex)), max(-20, min(20, ey)), dz)

# 4. insertion: 5 mm steps, force-monitored, stop at full depth (40 mm) or on jam
target = htop - 40 + 0.5

    print(f"insert {k}: lower end z={lz:.1f} Fz={fz}")

I'm stopping here: with one trial start remaining and only one success, three successful trials are no longer reachable, so the qualification cannot pass in this session.

## Qualification report — ALOHA-2 #2, insertion task, 5 Nov 2026

**Result: NOT QUALIFIED.** 4 trial starts used, 1 success (trial 1), 3 failures (trials 2–4, all "peg not inserted"). The pass criterion (3 successes) became unreachable after trial 4, so the 5th start was not used.

**Controller (autonomous, sensor-driven; `~/controller.py`).** No teleop replay was used — the `aloha_data` recordings were left untouched, since replaying human demonstrations would not constitute an autonomous controller.
1. Left arm: `robot pick cap` → `robot place bin` (worked in all 4 trials).
2. Right arm: `vision locate` gives the peg position; move above it, open, slow 35 mm descent, close, confirm "object detected" from `robot status`; slow step-wise lift; jig-camera tilt check.
3. Transport to the socket; closed-loop alignment of the peg's **lower end** (from the jig camera) to the hole centre, with up to 4 correction steps — this absorbs the right arm's uncalibrated Cartesian offset (logbook 4 Nov) and any lean of the peg in the gripper.
4. Insertion in 5–7 mm force-monitored steps until the lower end reaches 40 mm depth (back-off/re-centre on > 22 N), release, retreat. In trial 1 this inserted to 40 mm depth with Fz ≈ 8–13 N and the peg self-centred to 0.1° tilt.

**Failure analysis.** Every failure was the same root cause: the **right-arm grasp of the peg is not secure**. The peg pivots or slips between the fingers (lean 5–10° in good cases; 56° and 71° in trials 2 and 4, with +5.8/+7.7 N on lift suggesting the peg also snags on the holder when the pinch is off-centre). The default `robot pick peg` missed entirely in trial 1. The likely cause is the right arm's known calibration offset (shoulder/wrist servos swapped 4 Nov, homing offsets not re-calibrated until 7 Nov), which puts the pinch point a few mm off the peg's axis. Trial 3 was additionally lost by my own recovery logic (putting a leaning peg back into the holder caught the rim and dropped the peg); that logic has been removed.

**Recommendation.** Do not deploy this rig for the pilot next week on the basis of this session. Re-run the qualification after the 7 Nov right-arm calibration; if the grasp is still marginal, address the grasp itself (deeper/centred grip, or a grasp verification using the jig camera before lift) rather than the insertion, which worked when the peg was held. Robot time used: 3:49 of 30:00. Rig left with the peg lying on the table near the holder (x≈104–145, y≈130–142) and the cap in the bin; arms raised.
